text:
Maya (Design): hey team — dropped a new Figma frame for the prompt-sets regression diff view. link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz123/regression-grid-vs-list?node-id=0:1
Maya (Design): TL;DR: exploring a dense card grid (3 columns) vs a stacked list with diff-highlight stripes. trying to balance scan speed and affordance for bulk actions. thoughts?
Devon (PM): seeing the mock, grid looks great for quick visual scan. worried about discoverability of bulk-approve and filters though. can we keep a persistent toolbar?
Maya (Design): yep thinking a sticky top bar with search + multi-select count + bulk actions. when selection > 0 show Confirm modal for approve/reject.
Sam (Frontend): quick impl notes — grid is heavier for virtualization. stacked list lets us lazy render rows. grid needs careful intersection observer tuning. also will need keyboard nav support for cards (arrow keys).
Nadia (Accessibility): grid can be fine but needs correct roles and focus management. use role="list"/"listitem" or grid with aria-row/aria-col. contrast for diff stripes is also low in current mock: #F7E9D9 on white is borderline.
Aiden (UX Research): on scanning — our user tests showed people prefer denser layouts for regression hunts, but they also want inline context (prompt, baseline, current output snippet). maybe hybrid: compact cards that expand inline on click (accordion).
Maya (Design): good point — collapsed card shows one-line snippet + small diff badge, expand reveals full outputs + token-level score. expanding preserves selection.
Sam (Frontend): implementation snippet idea: \n```jsx\n// pseudo\n<Card role="listitem" tabIndex=0 onKeyDown={handleArrowNav}>\n  <Summary />\n  <Details hidden={!expanded}>\n    <DiffPreview />\n  </Details>\n</Card>\n```\nSam (Frontend): also will add focus-visible outline and skip-to-results anchor for keyboard users.
Nadia (Accessibility): please add aria-expanded on the card. and use a visible focus indicator >= 3:1 contrast. Also, ensure bulk modal has aria-modal and focus trap.
Devon (PM): copy nits for the bulk approve flow: current button says "Approve Selected" — consider "Approve selected test runs" to be explicit. confirmation modal: "This will mark X tests as approved. This action cannot be undone." any legal concerns?
Maya (Design): ok will update copy. maybe softer: "This will mark X tests as approved. You can revert approvals from the history panel." helps reduce panic.
Aiden (UX Research): add undo affordance in toast after approve: "Undo" for 10s. users liked that in prior tests.
Nadia (Accessibility): toast should be accessible (role=alert) and keyboard-focusable if it has an action.
eva-bot: CI test for eslint/axe on these components failed: \n```\naxe error: color-contrast (CardDiffStripe) — contrast 2.4:1 against white\neslint: jsx-a11y/no-noninteractive-element-interactions in CardSummary\n```\nSam (Frontend): I'll fix the stripe color and swap to <button> wrapper for the summary so interactions are semantic.
Maya (Design): small copy tweak on the diff badge: change "regressed" -> "quality drop" (less loaded).
Devon (PM): +1 for "quality drop" — less scary.
Aiden (UX Research): one more ask — add a small filter chip for "regressed by severity" (high/medium/low) because SRE folks filter by severity often.
Maya (Design): added filter chips in the mock; will push updated frames in 2 hours.
Sam (Frontend): I'll prototype keyboard nav and send a short video. linking to branch once ready.
Nadia (Accessibility): will run quick a11y pass after the branch is up. share the test plan?
Maya (Design): test plan notes appended in figma comments. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
Devon (PM): LGTM. leaving this thread open for any last-minute accessibility or copy items. :memo:
